Carrier C v10 · Browser controls + Android app 1.2.0 · SCOUT 2

Scout Web Control
and Firmware Guide

Drive Scout with a virtual joystick over its own Wi-Fi network. The ESP32-C3 serves its own controller: joystick, speed limit, Stop, saved motor directions and animated OLED face buttons. Open it from a phone, tablet or computer on Scout Wi-Fi. Browser updates run every 100 ms, replies time out after 800 ms, and the ESP stops browser driving after one second without a valid command. Android retains its 400 ms cutoff.

Drive Scout from a web browser

No app installation is required. Scout serves the controller itself, so a phone, tablet or computer can drive over its local Wi-Fi. Keep the controller tab visible and use one controller at a time.

  1. Before connecting ESP USB or uploading firmware, keep RUN OPEN/OFF. The current firmware is included in the software download.
  2. Before powered driving, unplug ESP USB, lift the wheels for the first direction check, then close RUN.
  3. Join C3-Scout-Test, password ScoutTest42. Choose to stay connected even though it has no Internet.
  4. Open http://192.168.4.1/ in your browser, then press Connect. This address works while connected to Scout, not from the public Internet.
  5. Start at the default 35% drive limit. Drag the joystick to move and release to send zero. Press Stop to end the session; reconnect deliberately to drive again.

Controls and animated faces

The page includes the joystick, speed limit, motor targets and a pinned Stop button. Expand Motor directions after stopping to save each motor’s reverse setting. On this Scout both reverse flags are ON; a normal firmware upload preserves them.

Choose Auto to cycle all ten expressions, or choose Happy, Laughing, Surprised, Angry, Sad, Sleepy, Skeptical, Winking, Cheeky or Dizzy. The eyes keep blinking and looking around while driving. Swipe the face row to see every choice. The 128×64 SSD1306 uses SDA GPIO5, SCL GPIO7, 3V3 and GND; the tested address is 0x3C. If the OLED is unavailable, the controller disables the face buttons while retaining motor control.

19 October steering and connection update

Reverse turns now follow the intended steering direction. Straight forward/reverse travel and turning on the spot retain their confirmed mapping. Keep both saved motor reverse flags ON for this Scout.

The browser sends the current joystick command every 100 ms without waiting for each earlier reply. Its reply timeout is 800 ms. Browser sessions on the ESP expire after 1 second without an accepted drive command; Android sessions retain their existing 400 ms timeout. Release sends zero immediately, and Stop ends the session immediately when received. After a lost connection the motors may continue for up to one second before the ESP cutoff.

Operator feedback: after the timing update, Scout is reported to be working “way better,” and the direction is confirmed correct. This is a successful driving check, not a range or endurance qualification. Reload the controller page after updating firmware to load the current steering and timing. If a session expires or replies are delayed, check Scout Wi-Fi and press Connect deliberately; movement never automatically resumes.

A hidden page, lost focus, a browser UI stalled for more than 250 ms, missing replies or excessive send backlog still ends control. Face selection does not renew the motor lease. Release blocks a new movement until its zero command is acknowledged. Duplicate, future and stale replies cannot keep a session alive.

What was verified

  • Twelve browser regression test groups, 310 firmware host checks, Android compatibility suites and browser layouts at 390×844, 375×667 and 844×390 passed. Tests cover 600 ms reply latency, the 100 ms update interval, exact timeout boundaries, release, Stop and controller ownership.
  • The installed build uses 1,182,293 bytes of application flash and 40,792 bytes of static RAM. Flash hashes verified on COM3; serial checks confirmed ready, OLED ready, zero motor targets, driver disabled, preserved calibration and the 1000 ms browser timeout.
  • The operator confirms improved wireless driving after installation. Longer wireless stress, range and endurance tests remain separate work.

Build and compatibility

The download includes the current ESP firmware, browser sources and tests, Android app 1.2.0, and ScoutFaces 1.0.0. The Android app uses the same single-controller session and protocol 2. Stop the current controller before switching between app and browser.

Install Arduino WebSockets 2.7.2, Adafruit SSD1306/GFX and the included ScoutFaces library. The build helper generates the compressed page from source/firmware/web before compiling. The ESP serves HTTP on port 80, browser drive on WebSocket port 81, and retains UDP 4210 for the Android app. Source and build instructions are included below; local tool paths may need adjustment on another computer.

Android app setup (optional)

  1. Before programming: open RUN or remove its jumper before connecting the ESP module's USB port to the computer. Load the matching SCOUT 2 firmware.
  2. Install Scout-Control-debug.apk on the Android phone. It is a debug-signed test build; Android may ask you to allow installation from the app opening the APK.
  3. Before powering the motors: unplug the ESP USB cable, lift the wheels clear for the first direction check, then close RUN. Keep RUN open while charging or programming; this carrier has no charge-and-run load sharing.
  4. Open Scout, tap Connect, grant the requested Wi-Fi permission, and approve C3-Scout-Test in Android's prompt. On Android 10–12, also turn on the phone's Location switch. The app does not read GPS location.
  5. For Android 8–9, join C3-Scout-Test manually first, using password ScoutTest42, and choose to stay connected without Internet.
  6. Start at the default 35% drive limit. Push up for forward, down for reverse, or sideways to turn. Release to stop. At full forward travel, 35% requests about 44% motor power.
  7. Press STOP to end the session. Tap Connect for a new session; it begins at zero and requires a new joystick touch.

Use Android app 1.2.0 with SCOUT 2 / protocol 2. TEST 04 and SCOUT 1 are earlier firmware and do not support this app's packet drive channel.

Direction settings

Steering correction in app 1.2.0. After both motor directions were reversed, the original steering mix turned the wrong way. This patch reverses only the steering differential: steering = turn while moving forward or turning on the spot, and −turn while reversing; left = forward − steering, right = forward + steering, before power mapping. Straight forward and reverse commands are unchanged. Keep both saved reverse flags ON for this Scout. The browser correction requires the current ESP firmware; the included APK also contains the reverse-turn correction.

The tested Scout had forward and reverse swapped with the initial motor wiring. Both saved motor-direction switches are now ON: Reverse left motor and Reverse right motor. Saving and reading the settings back from the board confirmed the change.

  1. Press Stop, then open Motor directions.
  2. For this Scout, enable both reverse switches and tap Save directions.
  3. Reconnect and check forward with the wheels lifted. Other builds may need different settings depending on motor wiring.

The ESP stores these flags in nonvolatile storage under scout-motors, using keys leftReverse and rightReverse. A fresh or erased board defaults both flags to OFF. A normal application upload preserves them. Calibration is accepted only while the drive session is ended and the motor outputs are disabled.

Motor targets in the app remain signed forward/reverse commands; the saved flags determine the physical pin polarity. The direction correction is configuration, not a different firmware binary.

Board and wiring

This software targets the ESP32-C3 SuperMini on Carrier C v10, using the TC1508A motor driver through the TXU0104 level translator. The carrier uses one 18650 cell and two geared N20 motors. Earlier module-wiring examples are superseded by this carrier pin assignment.

ConnectionESP pinUse
Left motor, J2GPIO 0 and GPIO 1Opposite TC1508A inputs for direction and PWM
Right motor, J3GPIO 3 and GPIO 10Opposite TC1508A inputs for direction and PWM
Driver/translator enableGPIO 6Active high; low at startup, Stop and expiration
Motor PWMFour output channels10 kHz, 8-bit duty, one direction input active per motor

Use the Carrier C v10 factory guide for the electrical files and the Scout project index for Rev B mechanical models. The completed mechanical model is still identified separately from Carrier C electrical placement.

Open RUN before attaching the ESP USB cable. Unplug ESP USB before closing RUN. Opening RUN provides a physical motor-power cut independent of the app; the software Stop button is not a physical emergency-stop circuit.

Expansion reference · 16 October 2026

Adding an OLED and sensors

The ESP32-C3 Super Mini exposes 13 GPIOs. Carrier C v10 uses five for motor control and connects one to battery-voltage sensing, leaving seven GPIOs unused by the carrier. Four are the preferred expansion choices: GPIO5, GPIO7, GPIO20 and GPIO21. The other three—GPIO2, GPIO8 and GPIO9—have startup restrictions.

Open the pinout at full size · Download the editable SVG. On a phone, scroll the diagram sideways to read the labels.

Which pins can we use?

GPIOStatus on ScoutExpansion guidance
5, 7AvailableRecommended I²C pair: GPIO5 = SDA, GPIO7 = SCL. Neither is wired to a carrier circuit.
20, 21Available, with serial caveatAlso UART RX and TX. SCOUT 2 uses USB CDC for its console, so it does not allocate these pins. GPIO21 can emit boot messages before the application starts; avoid connecting an actuator that would respond to them.
2, 8, 9ConditionalBoot-strapping pins: attached devices must not force an incorrect level during reset. GPIO8 also drives the usual Super Mini onboard LED; GPIO9 connects to BOOT. Leave these unused for the first expansion. Verify the exact module variant before repurposing them.
4Reserved for voltage sensingAlready wired to the 330 kΩ / 100 kΩ divider and 100 nF filter. It senses the switched VMOTOR rail, approximately battery voltage while RUN is closed. Current firmware does not read it; it is not a spare digital pin.
0, 1 / 3, 10 / 6In useLeft motor / right motor / driver enable. Keep these connections dedicated to motor control.

Recommended four-wire I²C OLED connection

Use a four-pin I²C OLED module rated for 3.3 V power and logic, for example an appropriate SSD1306 module. Check the labels on that display: the order of its VCC and GND pins varies between products. The table gives signal names, not a universal connector order.

OLED pinConnect to Super MiniPurpose
VCC / VIN3V3Regulated 3.3 V power; carrier test pad TP6 is on the same net
GNDGNDCommon ground; carrier test pad TP1 is on the same net
SDAGPIO5I²C data
SCLGPIO7I²C clock

No dedicated sensor or OLED connector is fitted on Carrier C v10. Attach a short harness to the module header pins or their carrier solder joints. If the module is socketed, a suitable header interposer is another option. Match the printed pin labels before soldering; the underside view is mirrored. Insulate the joints, provide strain relief, and keep wiring away from the motors and antenna.

Power and logic: use 3V3 and GND for the proposed OLED. The pin marked 5V is the carrier's ESP_5V supply rail, downstream of its series diode; its battery-powered voltage can be below 5 V. It is not a GPIO or a 3.3 V logic connection. Do not connect 5 V pull-ups or 5 V sensor outputs directly to the ESP GPIOs. Check the actual module regulator's available current before adding multiple peripherals; no spare-current budget has been qualified for this assembly.

Power off and disconnect the battery and USB before attaching wires. Preserve Scout's existing power procedure: RUN open before ESP USB is connected; ESP USB disconnected before RUN is closed. Use the board's common GND, not the cell's BAT_MINUS terminal, for peripherals.

Firmware changes and future sensors

The current SCOUT 2 firmware operates the 128×64 SSD1306 OLED with animated ScoutFaces on GPIO5/SDA and GPIO7/SCL. External sensor integration is still future work. An OLED update needs the appropriate display library, an explicit I²C pin assignment and the actual display address. For the wiring above, the bus initialization would be:

#include <Wire.h>

// Inside setup(): SDA = GPIO5, SCL = GPIO7, initial bus speed = 100 kHz.
Wire.begin(5, 7, 100000);

This line only starts the bus; display initialization and drawing are additional. Keep bus operations and display refreshes bounded and outside the motor safety timer and critical sections. Handle a missing display without hanging the control loop. Verify neutral startup, disconnect handling and Stop again after any firmware change.

I²C sensors can share GPIO5/SDA and GPIO7/SCL with the OLED, provided their addresses do not conflict and their power and logic levels are compatible. Use pull-ups to 3.3 V only; modules often include them already, and several sets in parallel can become too strong. After adding the OLED, GPIO20 and GPIO21 remain available, plus the three conditional boot pins. For more digital inputs and outputs, an I²C GPIO expander is an option; keep motor-enable and other timing-critical functions on their existing direct GPIOs.

These counts describe digital I/O, not seven spare analog inputs. GPIO5's ADC2 has chip-revision restrictions; do not assume it is a usable analog input. An external I²C ADC is an option for analog sensors while preserving the existing motor and voltage-sensing connections.

Checked against the Carrier C v10 board, its schematic, and the released firmware. Technical references: Espressif I²C configuration, ESP32-C3 GPIO and boot requirements, ESP32-C3 datasheet and ADC restrictions, Super Mini pin order and onboard functions, and OLED power and logic requirements. Pin allocation has been checked from design files; the OLED addition has not been assembled or bench tested.

Forward-facing camera with attached USB adapter

ESP32-CAM print and assembly guide · Download camera package · Bumper STL · Rear support STL · Editable Fusion mount

The camera faces forward, with its antenna up and USB/microSD access below. Remove the rear support before inserting the assembled camera and adapter, then reinstall it and slide it into gentle contact with bare PCB edges. It is a locating stop, not a clamp for forcing the boards together. Small cable ties restrain the USB lead through the upright openings.

This prototype targets the HiLetgo ESP32-CAM kit. The camera PCB outline is documented, but the assembled USB-adapter stack and connector revision are not. The depth adjustment does not compensate for a board that is too wide or tall. Check component contact, retention and cable clearance against the detailed guide.

Camera power is a separate integration step. Do not power it from a C3 GPIO. Before connecting it to Scout’s battery system, verify regulator capacity and supply stability under motor load. Camera streaming and control-app integration are not included in this mechanical release.

The complete robot ZIP includes both options under 07-Bumper-Options/. The smaller software-only ZIP includes this guide; companion CAD files require a bumper package or the complete robot download.

Motor power mapping

The small gearmotors did not reliably turn below roughly 40% motor power. Each wheel's logical command, after joystick dead-zone handling, mixing and the drive limit, is mapped independently:

magnitude = abs(logical wheel command)
if magnitude <= 30:
    motor target = 0
else:
    motor magnitude = 40 + floor((magnitude - 30) * 60 / 70)
    motor target = original sign * motor magnitude
Logical wheel magnitudeMapped motor target
0–30%0% · off
31%40%
35%44%
40%48%
60%65%
65%70%
100%100%

Reverse uses the same magnitudes with the opposite sign. The threshold applies after mixing and the drive limit, so at the default 35% limit, movement starts near the outer part of joystick travel. The L/R labels display the mapped targets, not measured speed.

The app sends physical motor targets; firmware does not apply the mapping a second time. It independently clamps physical targets below 40% to zero. Every nonzero PWM value is at least 102/255, including the 200 ms acceleration ramp. A direction change holds both inputs low for at least 100 ms before applying opposite power. There is no full-power startup kick.

Android connection and stopping

Android joysticklatest left/right pair
→
Wi-Fi · UDP 4210commands about every 50 ms
→
ESP motor loopPWM and enable gate

Scout is its own access point: C3-Scout-Test, password ScoutTest42, IP 192.168.4.1. It uses Wi-Fi, not Bluetooth, and needs no cloud account or Internet connection. These are shared development credentials embedded in both source trees; changing them requires updating both builds.

Android 10 and later use an exact-network request and bind the control sockets to Scout's Wi-Fi. The app retains this request while visible. A normal Stop ends the motor session while retaining Wi-Fi for quick reconnect or calibration. Leaving the app stops the session and releases the request. Later radio recovery never automatically resumes driving.

HTTP handles setup, status and calibration in a separate ESP task. Continuous driving uses UDP to avoid the HTTP stalls reproduced on the test phone. A random session token and increasing sequence reject old or foreign drive commands. Acknowledgements also include the board's boot identity.

ConditionResponse
Joystick releasedAn urgent zero pair takes priority over a rapid new touch
Stop pressedThree global Stop packets plus an independent HTTP Stop attempt; token revoked
No accepted drive command for 400 msIndependent ESP timer disables the driver and ends the session
No fresh valid acknowledgement for 400 msApp ends the session and requires reconnect
App UI stale for more than 250 msHeld input is discarded; reconnect required
App paused, hidden, or active window loses focusSession is ended; repeated lifecycle exits share one cleanup
Firmware setup or PWM faultNot ready; outputs remain disabled

The ESP checks expiration every 10 ms independently of web requests. This is a software cutoff with scheduler and hardware response time, not a certified stop-time guarantee. The board has no wheel encoders, battery telemetry, or current feedback in this release.

On Android 13 and later, grant Nearby devices; on Android 10–12, grant the Wi-Fi-related Location permission and turn Location on.

ESP firmware

In Arduino IDE, open source/firmware/ScoutDrive/ScoutDrive.ino with both headers in the same folder. Select ESP32C3 Dev Module with USB CDC On Boot enabled. Or use Arduino CLI with the listed core installed:

arduino-cli compile --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32c3:CDCOnBoot=cdc --output-dir firmware/output firmware/ScoutDrive

# RUN must be OPEN before ESP USB is connected. Replace COM3 with your port:
arduino-cli upload --fqbn esp32:esp32:esp32c3:CDCOnBoot=cdc --port COM3 --input-dir firmware/output firmware/ScoutDrive

The PowerShell firmware helper accepts -ArduinoCli and -ArduinoData; its defaults describe the original development computer, so set them to your installed toolchain. The guarded upload helper expects its matching generated configuration:

./scripts/build-firmware.ps1 -ArduinoCli "C:\Tools\arduino-cli.exe" -ArduinoData "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Arduino15"
./scripts/upload-firmware.ps1 -Port COM3 -RunOpenAndEspUsbConnected -ArduinoCli "C:\Tools\arduino-cli.exe"

Use a normal application upload to preserve motor calibration. Do not erase the whole flash unless you intend to reset saved settings. After a fresh flash, set both direction switches ON for the wiring used on this Scout.

Host checks

./android/test-host.ps1
./firmware/test-host.ps1

The firmware host script uses MSVC and accepts a toolchain path through scripts/test-firmware.ps1 -MsvcRoot. It builds a minimal Windows import library rather than requiring the full Windows SDK. Local HTTP tests need permission to open loopback sockets.

Protocol reference

Protocol 2 pairs SCOUT 2 firmware and app 1.1. HTTP is local cleartext on port 80; drive traffic and acknowledgements use UDP port 4210. The token prevents stale sessions from controlling the motors; it is not encryption.

HTTP endpointPurpose
GET /statusRead version, readiness, boot identity, session state, mapped targets, direction flags and timeout
POST /session · empty bodyOpen a neutral session and return its 32-character hexadecimal token; reject another live session
POST /stopGlobal Stop and token invalidation; available even if extra fields are supplied
POST /configForm fields leftReversed=0|1, rightReversed=0|1; session must be ended
POST /driveRetained diagnostic handler with token, seq, left, right; the app uses UDP instead

Status includes protocol, version, drivePort, boot, ready, connected, enabled, left, right, leftReversed, rightReversed, timeoutMs and message. Only the session response adds token.

Drive packet · 45 bytes

Byte offsetLengthField
04ASCII SCT2
41D drive or S global Stop
532Lowercase hexadecimal session token; app Stop uses 32 zeros
374Unsigned sequence; drive starts at 1 and increases
412Signed left motor percentage, −100 to +100
432Signed right motor percentage, −100 to +100

Acknowledgement · 50 bytes

Byte offsetLengthField
04ASCII ACK2
432Echoed token
364Echoed unsigned sequence
401Result: 0 accepted, 1 conflict, 2 invalid, 3 unavailable
414Unsigned boot identity
451Flags: ready 1, connected 2, enabled 4
462Left requested target
482Right requested target

All multibyte integers use big-endian network order. Malformed drive frames are discarded. Expired, wrong-token or non-increasing drive commands cannot renew the lease. Reordered acknowledgements cannot renew the app's reply timer. Stop invalidates the token, so a delayed drive packet cannot restart an ended session.

Troubleshooting

SymptomAction
Scout does not appear in Android's promptCheck robot power, Wi-Fi permission, and Location on Android 10–12. Cancel a stale prompt, then retry Connect.
Connected, no InternetExpected for Scout's local network. Stay connected; Internet is not required to drive.
Link ends or replies are lostStop, check robot power and distance, then reconnect. Motors do not automatically resume when the radio returns.
Firmware update neededInstall matching SCOUT 2; app 1.2.0 does not drive SCOUT 1 or TEST 04.
Motors remain still at low inputLogical wheel targets at or below 30% are intentionally off. Start at 35% with full joystick travel, then raise the limit gradually if needed.
Forward runs backwardStop and adjust Motor directions. On the tested Scout, both reverse switches are ON.
One wheel runs backwardChange only that wheel's saved reverse flag and repeat the wheels-lifted direction check.
Another live session existsPress Stop, then reconnect. A stopped or expired session's old token cannot be reused.

ScoutFaces: reusable animated OLED library

Give a future OLED project Scout’s ten funny faces, with blinking and glances. Oversized eyes, eyebrows, a small nose and expressive mouths fill the 128 × 64 screen. Each expression lasts about six seconds before the next one appears.

Download ScoutFaces 1.0.0 Arduino library · includes editable source, artwork, API documentation and two example sketches.

Install and try it

  1. Download the ZIP above. In Arduino IDE select Sketch → Include Library → Add .ZIP Library… and choose it.
  2. Install Adafruit SSD1306 and Adafruit GFX Library with their dependencies through Library Manager.
  3. Open File → Examples → ScoutFaces → AutoCycle. Choose your board and set its SDA/SCL pins. The example is configured for Scout’s ESP32-C3: SDA GPIO5, SCL GPIO7, 3V3 and GND. It checks 0x3C and 0x3D; Scout’s OLED responds at 0x3C.
  4. For Scout, keep RUN OPEN before connecting ESP USB and enable USB CDC On Boot. The examples hold motor enable GPIO6 LOW. Remove that Scout-specific pin assignment on other boards when appropriate. Uploading a demo replaces the drive firmware; restore ScoutDrive when you want phone driving again. Unplug ESP USB before RUN ON.

Add it to your own sketch

Create and initialize your display as usual, then bind the library to it. Call update() regularly; flush the driver’s framebuffer only when it returns true.

#include <Wire.h>
#include <Adafruit_SSD1306.h>
#include <ScoutFaces.h>

Adafruit_SSD1306 display(128, 64, &Wire, -1, 100000, 100000);
ScoutFaces faces(display);

void setup() {
  // ESP32 pin setup. Adapt this call for other board families.
  Wire.begin(5, 7, 100000);
  if (!display.begin(SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC, 0x3C, false, false)
      || !faces.begin()) while (true) delay(1000);
}

void loop() {
  if (faces.update()) display.display();
  // Other application work goes here.
}

The integration snippet assumes your project already handles any motor-enable pins. For a standalone Scout test use the supplied examples, which explicitly disable its motor driver.

Choose an expression or adjust timing

// Keep this expression, while its eyes continue to blink and glance:
faces.setExpression(ScoutFaces::Expression::Cheeky);

// Resume cycling from the current expression:
faces.setAutoCycle(true);

// Default timing: 48 ticks × 120 ms = 5.76 seconds per expression.
faces.setFrameInterval(120);
APIBehavior
begin()Starts the timeline; returns false unless display dimensions are 128 × 64 in landscape.
update()Draws only changed poses; returns true when you should flush the framebuffer. Does not initialize or communicate with hardware.
setExpression(expression)Selects one face and turns expression cycling off; eye animation continues. Resets its timeline.
setAutoCycle(true/false)Enables or disables expression cycling and restarts its timeline.
setFrameInterval(ms)Sets milliseconds per tick, minimum 20. Use 120 for the tested 100 kHz connection.
expression(), pose(), autoCycle()Read current state; expression/pose reflect the latest update.
ScoutFaces::name(expression), expressionCount()Get the expression name or the count of ten expressions.

Expression names: Happy, Laughing, Surprised, Angry, Sad, Sleepy, Skeptical, Winking, Cheeky, Dizzy. Prefix each with ScoutFaces::Expression::. See the ZIP’s README for clock arguments and pose names.

Compatibility and limits

Compiled for ESP32-C3 with Arduino ESP32 3.3.12, SSD1306 2.5.17 and GFX 1.12.6. Other 128 × 64 GFX framebuffer drivers can be bound to the renderer; their initialization and flush calls remain your responsibility. Artwork occupies 92,160 bytes of flash, so an ATmega328P Uno or classic Nano cannot hold it. Other boards need sufficient memory and their own Wire configuration.

The library has no animation delays or pin, Wire, Serial or motor calls. It clears the full framebuffer when drawing and skips missed poses if the main loop is late. Your display flush still takes about 100 ms at 100 kHz; keep it out of timing-critical motor control. Faster timing requires a faster compatible bus. Geometry checks do not detect missing hardware; check wiring and the address if the screen is blank. If frames never appear, confirm you call display.display() after a true update result.

The original animated demo ran a complete verified USB cycle on Scout. Packaging the library does not replace the firmware on the robot.

Complete firmware source

The sketch and headers below include the current browser controller, OLED integration and motor safety logic used to build SCOUT 2. Expand a file to read or copy it. The download contains the same files under source/firmware/ScoutDrive.

firmware/ScoutDrive/BrowserControl.h

Download this source file

#pragma once
#include "DriveDatagram.h"
#include "FaceControl.h"
namespace scout {
constexpr uint32_t BROWSER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 1000;
enum class WebAction { Connect, Stop, Face };
struct WebCommand { WebAction action; int face = -1; };
inline bool parseWebText(const uint8_t* bytes, unsigned size, WebCommand& command) {
  if (!bytes) return false;
  if (size == 1 && (bytes[0] == 'C' || bytes[0] == 'S')) {
    command.action = bytes[0] == 'C' ? WebAction::Connect : WebAction::Stop;
    return true;
  }
  if ((size == 3 || size == 4) && bytes[0] == 'F' && bytes[1] == ',') {
    char id[3] = {char(bytes[2]), size == 4 ? char(bytes[3]) : char(0), 0};
    if (parseFaceId(id, command.face)) { command.action = WebAction::Face; return true; }
  }
  return false;
}
// Call under safetyMux. Socket ownership is in addition to the session token;
// delayed disconnects cannot affect a newer browser or Android session.
struct BrowserControl {
  int owner = -1;
  char token[33] = {};
  bool matches(const DriveCore& core, uint8_t client) const {
    if (owner != client || !core.connected) return false;
    for (unsigned i = 0; i != 33; ++i) if (token[i] != core.token[i]) return false;
    return true;
  }
  bool owns(const DriveCore& core, uint8_t client, uint64_t now) const {
    return matches(core, client) && core.ready && now < core.deadline;
  }
  Result claim(DriveCore& core, uint8_t client, const char* fresh, uint64_t now) {
    const Result result = core.session(fresh, now, BROWSER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS);
    if (result == Result::Ok) {
      owner = client;
      for (unsigned i = 0; i != 33; ++i) token[i] = fresh[i];
    }
    return result;
  }
  Result drive(DriveCore& core, uint8_t client, const DrivePacket& packet, uint64_t now) {
    if (packet.stop) return Result::Invalid;
    if (!owns(core, client, now)) return Result::Conflict;
    return core.drive(packet.token, packet.sequence, packet.left, packet.right, now);
  }
  bool release(DriveCore& core, uint8_t client, uint64_t now) {
    const bool owned = matches(core, client);
    if (owned) core.stop(now);
    if (owner == client) { owner = -1; token[0] = 0; }
    return owned;
  }
};
}

#pragma once
#include <stdint.h>
namespace scout {
enum class Result { Ok, Invalid, Conflict, Unavailable };
struct Motor {
  int requested = 0;
  int pwm = 0;
  int lastDirection = 0, rampFrom = 0;
  uint64_t lowSince = 0, deadUntil = 0, rampAt = 0;
  static int sign(int n) { return (n > 0) - (n < 0); }
  static int magnitude(int n) { return n < 0 ? -n : n; }
  void cut(uint64_t now) {
    if (pwm != 0) lowSince = now;
    pwm = 0;
  }
  void advance(uint64_t now) {
    if (!requested || now < rampAt || now < deadUntil) { cut(now); return; }
    const int goal = (magnitude(requested) * 255 + 50) / 100;
    const uint64_t elapsed = now - rampAt;
    const int base = rampFrom < 102 ? 102 : rampFrom; // 40% PWM: never energize in the stalled low range.
    const int64_t change = (goal - base) * static_cast<int64_t>(elapsed);
    const int duty = elapsed >= 200 ? goal : base +
      static_cast<int>((change + (change < 0 ? -100 : 100)) / 200);
    pwm = sign(requested) * duty;
    if (pwm) lastDirection = sign(pwm);
  }
  void target(int value, uint64_t now) {
    if (magnitude(value) < 40) value = 0;
    advance(now);
    if (value == requested) return; // Repeated samples never restart a ramp.
    if (!value) { stop(now); return; }
    const int direction = sign(value);
    if (lastDirection && direction != lastDirection) {
      cut(now);
      const uint64_t earliest = lowSince + 100;
      if (earliest > deadUntil) deadUntil = earliest;
    }
    rampFrom = magnitude(pwm);
    if (!requested || direction != sign(requested) || now < deadUntil) rampFrom = 0;
    rampAt = now < deadUntil ? deadUntil : now;
    requested = value;
  }
  void stop(uint64_t now) { cut(now); requested = rampFrom = 0; }
};
struct DriveCore {
  bool ready = false, connected = false;
  uint64_t deadline = 0;
  uint32_t commandTimeoutMs = 400;
  uint32_t sequence = 0, generation = 0;
  char token[33] = {};
  Motor motors[2];
  bool expire(uint64_t now) {
    if (!connected || now < deadline) return false;
    stop(now); return true;
  }
  void stop(uint64_t now) { connected = false; token[0] = 0; motors[0].stop(now); motors[1].stop(now); ++generation; }
  Result session(const char* freshToken, uint64_t now, uint32_t timeoutMs = 400) {
    expire(now);
    if (!ready) return Result::Unavailable;
    if (connected) return Result::Conflict;
    stop(now);
    for (unsigned i = 0; i != 32; ++i) token[i] = freshToken[i];
    commandTimeoutMs = timeoutMs;
    token[32] = 0; sequence = 0; deadline = now + commandTimeoutMs; connected = true;
    return Result::Ok;
  }
  Result drive(const char* supplied, uint32_t seq, int left, int right, uint64_t now) {
    expire(now);
    if (left < -100 || left > 100 || right < -100 || right > 100) return Result::Invalid;
    if (!ready) return Result::Unavailable;
    if (!connected || !seq || seq <= sequence) return Result::Conflict;
    unsigned i = 0;
    while (i < 32 && supplied[i] && supplied[i] == token[i]) ++i;
    if (i != 32 || supplied[32] != 0) return Result::Conflict;
    motors[0].target(left, now); motors[1].target(right, now);
    sequence = seq; deadline = now + commandTimeoutMs;
    return Result::Ok;
  }
  void advance(uint64_t now) { expire(now); motors[0].advance(now); motors[1].advance(now); }
  bool canEnable(uint64_t now) const {
    return ready && connected && now < deadline && (motors[0].pwm || motors[1].pwm);
  }
};
inline bool parseSequence(const char* text, uint32_t& result) {
  if (!text || !*text) return false;
  uint32_t value = 0;
  for (; *text; ++text) {
    if (*text < '0' || *text > '9') return false;
    const uint32_t digit = *text - '0';
    if (value > (UINT32_MAX - digit) / 10) return false;
    value = value * 10 + digit;
  }
  result = value; return true;
}
inline bool parsePercent(const char* text, int& result) {
  if (!text) return false;
  const bool negative = *text == '-';
  uint32_t value;
  if (!parseSequence(text + (negative ? 1 : 0), value) || value > 100) return false;
  result = negative ? -static_cast<int>(value) : static_cast<int>(value); return true;
}
}

#pragma once
#include "DriveCore.h"
namespace scout {
constexpr unsigned DRIVE_PACKET_SIZE = 45, ACK_PACKET_SIZE = 50;
struct DrivePacket { bool stop; char token[33]; uint32_t sequence; int left, right; };
inline uint32_t read32(const uint8_t* b) { return (uint32_t(b[0])<<24)|(uint32_t(b[1])<<16)|(uint32_t(b[2])<<8)|b[3]; }
inline int read16(const uint8_t* b) { unsigned n = (unsigned(b[0])<<8)|b[1]; return n >= 32768 ? int(n)-65536 : int(n); }
inline void write32(uint8_t* b, uint32_t n) { b[0]=uint8_t(n>>24); b[1]=uint8_t(n>>16); b[2]=uint8_t(n>>8); b[3]=uint8_t(n); }
inline void write16(uint8_t* b, int n) { b[0]=uint8_t(unsigned(n)>>8); b[1]=uint8_t(n); }
inline bool decodeDrive(const uint8_t* b, unsigned size, DrivePacket& p) {
  if (size!=DRIVE_PACKET_SIZE || b[0]!='S'||b[1]!='C'||b[2]!='T'||b[3]!='2'||(b[4]!='D'&&b[4]!='S')) return false;
  p.stop=b[4]=='S';
  for (unsigned i=0;i<32;++i) { char c=char(b[5+i]); if (!((c>='0'&&c<='9')||(c>='a'&&c<='f'))) return false; p.token[i]=c; }
  p.token[32]=0; p.sequence=read32(b+37); p.left=read16(b+41); p.right=read16(b+43);
  return (p.stop || p.sequence!=0) && p.left>=-100&&p.left<=100&&p.right>=-100&&p.right<=100;
}
inline void encodeAck(uint8_t* b, const DrivePacket& p, uint8_t code, uint32_t boot, uint8_t flags, int left, int right) {
  b[0]='A';b[1]='C';b[2]='K';b[3]='2';
  for(unsigned i=0;i<32;++i)b[4+i]=uint8_t(p.token[i]);
  write32(b+36,p.sequence);b[40]=code;write32(b+41,boot);b[45]=flags;write16(b+46,left);write16(b+48,right);
}
}

#pragma once
#include "DriveCore.h"

namespace scout {
inline bool parseFaceId(const char* text, int& id) {
  if (!text) return false;
  if (text[0] == '-' && text[1] == '1' && text[2] == 0) { id = -1; return true; }
  if (text[0] >= '0' && text[0] <= '9' && text[1] == 0) { id = text[0] - '0'; return true; }
  return false;
}
// All access is protected by the firmware's safetyMux. No display/IO calls here.
struct FaceControl {
  bool available = false;
  int selection = -1;
  uint32_t generation = 0;
  Result select(const DriveCore& drive, const char* supplied, int id, uint64_t now) {
    if (id < -1 || id > 9) return Result::Invalid;
    if (!drive.ready || !drive.connected || now >= drive.deadline || !supplied)
      return Result::Conflict;
    unsigned i = 0;
    while (i < 32 && supplied[i] && supplied[i] == drive.token[i]) ++i;
    if (i != 32 || supplied[32] != 0) return Result::Conflict;
    if (!available) return Result::Unavailable;
    selection = id;
    ++generation;
    return Result::Ok;
  }
};
}

// Scout protocol 2 / Carrier C v10 / ESP32-C3 / Arduino ESP32 core 3.x.
#include <Arduino.h>
#include <WiFi.h>
#include <WebServer.h>
#include <WiFiUdp.h>
#include <Preferences.h>
#include <esp_timer.h>
#include <esp_random.h>
#include <driver/gpio.h>
#include "DriveCore.h"
#include "FaceControl.h"
#include "DriveDatagram.h"
#include <Wire.h>
#include <Adafruit_SSD1306.h>
#include <ScoutFaces.h>
#include <WebSocketsServer.h>
#include "BrowserControl.h"
#include "WebControlPage.h"

constexpr uint8_t ENABLE_PIN = 6;
constexpr uint8_t MOTOR_PINS[4] = {0, 1, 3, 10};
WebServer server(80);
WebSocketsServer browserSocket(81);
WiFiUDP driveUdp;
Preferences settings;
esp_timer_handle_t watchdog = nullptr;
portMUX_TYPE safetyMux = portMUX_INITIALIZER_UNLOCKED;
scout::DriveCore control;
scout::FaceControl faceControl;
scout::BrowserControl browserControl;
bool attached[4] = {}, reversed[2] = {}, enabled = false;
uint32_t bootId;
const char* eventMessage = "Stopped / ready";

uint64_t nowMs() { return static_cast<uint64_t>(esp_timer_get_time()) / 1000; }

// Runs in the ESP timer task independently of WebServer and its blocking client.
// Never performs PWM, network, serial, allocation or flash work here.
void safetyTick(void*) {
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (control.expire(nowMs())) {
    gpio_set_level(static_cast<gpio_num_t>(ENABLE_PIN), 0);
    enabled = false;
    eventMessage = "Contact expired / stopped";
  }
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
}

void stopAll(const char* message) {
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  gpio_set_level(static_cast<gpio_num_t>(ENABLE_PIN), 0);
  enabled = false;
  control.stop(nowMs());
  eventMessage = message;
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i) if (attached[i]) ledcWrite(MOTOR_PINS[i], 0);
}

void updateOutputs() {
  int pwm[2]; bool directions[2]; uint32_t generation;
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (control.expire(nowMs())) {
    gpio_set_level(static_cast<gpio_num_t>(ENABLE_PIN), 0);
    enabled = false; eventMessage = "Contact expired / stopped";
  }
  control.advance(nowMs());
  pwm[0] = control.motors[0].pwm; pwm[1] = control.motors[1].pwm;
  directions[0] = reversed[0]; directions[1] = reversed[1];
  generation = control.generation;
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);

  // LEDC takes internal locks: keep those calls outside the short safety lock.
  bool ok = true;
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
    const bool reverse = (pwm[i] < 0) != directions[i];
    const uint8_t duty = static_cast<uint8_t>(pwm[i] < 0 ? -pwm[i] : pwm[i]);
    // Clear the opposite input before setting PWM; never assert both directions.
    if (attached[2*i + (reverse ? 0 : 1)]) ok = ledcWrite(MOTOR_PINS[2*i + (reverse ? 0 : 1)], 0) && ok;
    if (attached[2*i + (reverse ? 1 : 0)]) ok = ledcWrite(MOTOR_PINS[2*i + (reverse ? 1 : 0)], duty) && ok;
  }
  if (!ok) {
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); control.ready = false; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    stopAll("PWM fault / stopped"); return;
  }
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  // A trip during PWM writes changes generation and invalidates the token.
  // No stale PWM snapshot can re-enable the driver after stop or expiration.
  if (control.expire(nowMs())) eventMessage = "Contact expired / stopped";
  enabled = generation == control.generation && control.canEnable(nowMs());
  gpio_set_level(static_cast<gpio_num_t>(ENABLE_PIN), enabled ? 1 : 0);
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
}

String statusJson(const char* sessionToken = nullptr) {
  safetyTick(nullptr);
  bool isReady, connected, isEnabled, leftReverse, rightReverse;
  int left, right; const char* message;
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  isReady = control.ready; connected = control.connected; isEnabled = enabled;
  left = control.motors[0].requested; right = control.motors[1].requested;
  leftReverse = reversed[0]; rightReverse = reversed[1]; message = eventMessage;
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  String json; json.reserve(400);
  json = "{\"protocol\":2,\"version\":\"SCOUT 2\",\"drivePort\":4210,\"boot\":" + String(bootId);
  json += ",\"ready\":"; json += isReady ? "true" : "false";
  json += ",\"connected\":"; json += connected ? "true" : "false";
  json += ",\"enabled\":"; json += isEnabled ? "true" : "false";
  json += ",\"left\":" + String(left) + ",\"right\":" + String(right);
  json += ",\"leftReversed\":"; json += leftReverse ? "true" : "false";
  json += ",\"rightReversed\":"; json += rightReverse ? "true" : "false";
  json += ",\"timeoutMs\":400,\"message\":\""; json += message; json += '"';
  json += ",\"browserTimeoutMs\":" + String(scout::BROWSER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS);
  if (sessionToken) { json += ",\"token\":\""; json += sessionToken; json += '"'; }
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  const bool oledReady = faceControl.available;
  const int selectedFace = faceControl.selection;
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  json += ",\"faceControl\":true,\"oledReady\":";
  json += oledReady ? "true" : "false";
  json += ",\"face\":" + String(selectedFace) + ",\"browserControl\":true";
  return json + '}';
}

void sendStatus(const char* token);
void handleFace() {
  int id;
  const String token = server.arg("token"), text = server.arg("id");
  if (server.args() != 2 || !server.hasArg("token") || !server.hasArg("id") ||
      token.length() != 32 || !scout::parseFaceId(text.c_str(), id)) {
    error(400, "Expected session token and face id -1..9"); return;
  }
  safetyTick(nullptr);
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  const scout::Result result = faceControl.select(control, token.c_str(), id, nowMs());
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (result == scout::Result::Unavailable) { error(503, "OLED unavailable"); return; }
  if (result != scout::Result::Ok) { error(409, "Face selection needs the current drive session"); return; }
  sendStatus(nullptr);
}

// Optional low-priority task: neither the UDP loop nor lease timer waits on I2C.
// This task exclusively owns the driver, framebuffer, Wire and face animation.
void oledTask(void*) {
  Adafruit_SSD1306 oled(128, 64, &Wire, -1, 100000, 100000);
  ScoutFaces faces(oled);
  uint8_t address = 0;
  if (Wire.begin(5, 7, 100000)) {
    Wire.setTimeOut(20);
    for (uint8_t candidate : {0x3C, 0x3D}) {
      Wire.beginTransmission(candidate);
      if (Wire.endTransmission() == 0) { address = candidate; break; }
    }
  }
  bool ok = address && oled.begin(SSD1306_SWITCHCAPVCC, address, false, false) && faces.begin();
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); faceControl.available = ok; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  Serial.println(ok ? "OLED animated faces ready" : "OLED unavailable; driving remains available");
  uint32_t generation = 0xFFFFFFFF;
  while (ok) {
    int selected; uint32_t revision;
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    selected = faceControl.selection; revision = faceControl.generation;
    portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    if (revision != generation) {
      if (selected < 0) faces.setAutoCycle(true);
      else faces.setExpression(static_cast<ScoutFaces::Expression>(selected));
      generation = revision;
      Serial.printf("OLED selection: %d\n", selected);
    }
    if (faces.update()) {
      Wire.beginTransmission(address);
      ok = Wire.endTransmission() == 0;
      if (ok) oled.display();
    }
    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(5));
  }
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); faceControl.available = false; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  // Keep the task dormant after failure; reset Scout after repairing the wiring.
  for (;;) vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(2000));
}

void sendStatus(const char* token = nullptr) {
  server.sendHeader("Cache-Control", "no-store");
  server.send(200, "application/json", statusJson(token));
}
void error(int code, const char* message) {
  server.sendHeader("Cache-Control", "no-store");
  server.send(code, "application/json", String("{\"protocol\":2,\"message\":\"") + message + "\"}");
}
bool emptyForm() { if (server.args() == 0) return true; error(400, "Expected empty form"); return false; }

void makeSessionToken(char* token) {
  static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
  uint8_t random[16]; esp_fill_random(random, sizeof(random));
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 16; ++i) { token[2*i] = hex[random[i] >> 4]; token[2*i+1] = hex[random[i] & 15]; }
  token[32] = 0;
}
void handleSession() {
  if (!emptyForm()) return;
  char token[33]; makeSessionToken(token);
  safetyTick(nullptr);
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  const scout::Result result = control.session(token, nowMs());
  if (result == scout::Result::Ok) { enabled = false; gpio_set_level(static_cast<gpio_num_t>(ENABLE_PIN), 0); eventMessage = "Connected / stopped"; }
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (result == scout::Result::Unavailable) { error(503, "Motor setup unavailable"); return; }
  if (result != scout::Result::Ok) { error(409, "A live session already exists"); return; }
  sendStatus(token);
}

void handleDrive() {
  const String token = server.arg("token"), seqText = server.arg("seq");
  const String leftText = server.arg("left"), rightText = server.arg("right");
  uint32_t seq; int left, right;
  if (server.args() != 4 || !server.hasArg("token") || !server.hasArg("seq") ||
      !server.hasArg("left") || !server.hasArg("right") || token.length() != 32 ||
      !scout::parseSequence(seqText.c_str(), seq) ||
      !scout::parsePercent(leftText.c_str(), left) || !scout::parsePercent(rightText.c_str(), right)) {
    error(400, "Invalid drive fields"); return;
  }
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  const scout::Result result = control.drive(token.c_str(), seq, left, right, nowMs());
  if (result == scout::Result::Ok) eventMessage = (left || right) ? "Drive accepted" : "Centered / stopped";
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (result == scout::Result::Unavailable) { error(503, "Motor setup unavailable"); return; }
  if (result != scout::Result::Ok) { error(409, "Session expired, wrong token or old sequence"); return; }
  sendStatus();
}

void handleConfig() {
  const String left = server.arg("leftReversed"), right = server.arg("rightReversed");
  if (server.args() != 2 || (left != "0" && left != "1") || (right != "0" && right != "1")) {
    error(400, "Expected leftReversed and rightReversed as 0 or 1"); return;
  }
  safetyTick(nullptr);
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  const bool live = control.connected; const bool ready = control.ready;
  // Prevent a browser/Android session from claiming control during flash writes.
  if (!live && ready) control.ready = false;
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (live) { error(409, "End session before calibration"); return; }
  if (!ready) { error(503, "Motor setup unavailable"); return; }
  stopAll("Calibration / stopped");
  const bool l = left == "1", r = right == "1";
  const bool savedLeft = settings.putBool("leftReverse", l) == 1;
  const bool savedRight = settings.putBool("rightReverse", r) == 1;
  if (!savedLeft || !savedRight) {
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); control.ready = false; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    stopAll("Calibration save failed / stopped"); error(500, "Cannot save direction"); return;
  }
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); reversed[0] = l; reversed[1] = r; control.ready = true; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); eventMessage = "Calibration saved / stopped"; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); sendStatus();
}

// The web server may wait for a slow client. It never owns the motor loop.
void webTask(void*) {
  for (;;) { server.handleClient(); vTaskDelay(1); }
}

void socketStatus(uint8_t client, uint32_t ack, const char* token) {
  String json = statusJson(token);
  if (ack) { json.remove(json.length()-1); json += ",\"ack\":" + String(ack) + '}'; }
  browserSocket.sendTXT(client, json);
}
void socketError(uint8_t client, const char* message) {
  String json = String("{\"error\":\"") + message + "\"}";
  browserSocket.sendTXT(client, json);
}
void releaseBrowser(uint8_t client) {
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (browserControl.release(control, client, nowMs())) {
    gpio_set_level(static_cast<gpio_num_t>(ENABLE_PIN), 0);
    enabled = false; eventMessage = "Browser stopped / session ended";
  }
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
}
void socketEvent(uint8_t client, WStype_t type, uint8_t* payload, size_t length) {
  safetyTick(nullptr);
  if (type == WStype_DISCONNECTED) { releaseBrowser(client); return; }
  if (type == WStype_CONNECTED) { socketStatus(client, 0, nullptr); return; }
  if (type == WStype_BIN) {
    scout::DrivePacket packet;
    if (!scout::decodeDrive(payload, length, packet) || packet.stop) {
      releaseBrowser(client); socketError(client, "Invalid browser drive frame"); return;
    }
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    const scout::Result result = browserControl.drive(control, client, packet, nowMs());
    if (result == scout::Result::Ok) eventMessage = (packet.left || packet.right) ? "Browser drive accepted" : "Browser centered / stopped";
    portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    if (result != scout::Result::Ok) { socketError(client, "Session expired or command rejected · reconnect"); return; }
    socketStatus(client, packet.sequence, nullptr); return;
  }
  if (type != WStype_TEXT) {
    // Fragmented application messages are not part of this bounded protocol.
    if (type == WStype_FRAGMENT_TEXT_START || type == WStype_FRAGMENT_BIN_START ||
        type == WStype_FRAGMENT || type == WStype_FRAGMENT_FIN || type == WStype_ERROR)
      releaseBrowser(client);
    return;
  }
  scout::WebCommand command;
  if (!scout::parseWebText(payload, length, command)) {
    releaseBrowser(client); socketError(client, "Invalid browser command"); return;
  }
  if (command.action == scout::WebAction::Connect) {
    char token[33]; makeSessionToken(token);
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    const scout::Result result = browserControl.claim(control, client, token, nowMs());
    if (result == scout::Result::Ok) {
      gpio_set_level(static_cast<gpio_num_t>(ENABLE_PIN), 0);
      enabled = false; eventMessage = "Browser connected / stopped";
    }
    portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    if (result != scout::Result::Ok) { socketError(client, "Scout unavailable or another controller is connected"); return; }
    socketStatus(client, 0, token); return;
  }
  if (command.action == scout::WebAction::Stop) {
    releaseBrowser(client); socketStatus(client, 0, nullptr); return;
  }
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  const scout::Result result = browserControl.owns(control, client, nowMs()) ?
      faceControl.select(control, browserControl.token, command.face, nowMs()) : scout::Result::Conflict;
  portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  if (result != scout::Result::Ok) { socketError(client, "Face unavailable or session ended"); return; }
  socketStatus(client, 0, nullptr);
}
void browserTask(void*) {
  // Library IO can wait for a client. Only this task owns browserSocket;
  // the motor loop, OLED task and independent lease timer do not wait on it.
  for (;;) { browserSocket.loop(); vTaskDelay(1); }
}
void receiveDrive() {
  for (unsigned batch=0; batch<4; ++batch) {
    int size=driveUdp.parsePacket(); if (!size) return;
    uint8_t bytes[scout::DRIVE_PACKET_SIZE];
    if (size!=int(sizeof(bytes))) { while(driveUdp.available()) driveUdp.read(); continue; }
    IPAddress sender=driveUdp.remoteIP(); uint16_t port=driveUdp.remotePort();
    if (driveUdp.read(bytes,sizeof(bytes))!=int(sizeof(bytes))) continue;
    scout::DrivePacket packet;
    if (!scout::decodeDrive(bytes,sizeof(bytes),packet)) continue;
    scout::Result result=scout::Result::Ok;
    if (packet.stop) stopAll("STOP / session ended");
    else {
      portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
      result=control.drive(packet.token,packet.sequence,packet.left,packet.right,nowMs());
      if(result==scout::Result::Ok)eventMessage=(packet.left||packet.right)?"Drive accepted":"Centered / stopped";
      portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    }
    updateOutputs();
    uint8_t flags; int left,right;
    portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    flags=(control.ready?1:0)|(control.connected?2:0)|(enabled?4:0);
    left=control.motors[0].requested;right=control.motors[1].requested;
    portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
    uint8_t ack[scout::ACK_PACKET_SIZE];
    uint8_t code=result==scout::Result::Ok?0:result==scout::Result::Conflict?1:result==scout::Result::Invalid?2:3;
    scout::encodeAck(ack,packet,code,bootId,flags,left,right);
    if(driveUdp.beginPacket(sender,port)){driveUdp.write(ack,sizeof(ack));driveUdp.endPacket();}
  }
}

void setup() {
  digitalWrite(ENABLE_PIN, LOW); pinMode(ENABLE_PIN, OUTPUT);
  bootId = esp_random();
  bool setupOk = true;
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
    digitalWrite(MOTOR_PINS[i], LOW); pinMode(MOTOR_PINS[i], OUTPUT);
    attached[i] = ledcAttach(MOTOR_PINS[i], 10000, 8); setupOk = attached[i] && setupOk;
  }
  stopAll("Startup / stopped");
  const bool storageReady = settings.begin("scout-motors", false);
  setupOk = storageReady && setupOk;
  if (storageReady) { reversed[0] = settings.getBool("leftReverse", false); reversed[1] = settings.getBool("rightReverse", false); }
  esp_timer_create_args_t args = {}; args.callback = safetyTick; args.name = "scout_lease";
  setupOk = (esp_timer_create(&args, &watchdog) == ESP_OK) && setupOk;
  if (watchdog) setupOk = (esp_timer_start_periodic(watchdog, 10000) == ESP_OK) && setupOk;
  Serial.begin(115200);
  WiFi.mode(WIFI_AP);
  const bool wifiReady = WiFi.softAP("C3-Scout-Test", "ScoutTest42", 1, false, 2);
  const bool udpReady = wifiReady && driveUdp.begin(4210)==1;
  setupOk = udpReady && setupOk;
  portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux); control.ready = setupOk; portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);
  stopAll(setupOk ? "Stopped / ready" : "Setup failed / stopped");
  server.on("/", HTTP_GET, [] {
    server.sendHeader("Cache-Control", "no-store");
    server.sendHeader("Content-Encoding", "gzip");
    server.sendHeader("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff");
    server.send_P(200, "text/html; charset=utf-8", reinterpret_cast<const char*>(WEB_CONTROL_PAGE), sizeof(WEB_CONTROL_PAGE));
  });
  server.on("/status", HTTP_GET, [] { sendStatus(); });
  server.on("/session", HTTP_POST, handleSession);
  server.on("/drive", HTTP_POST, handleDrive);
  // Stop always cuts outputs, including when a caller supplies extra fields.
  server.on("/stop", HTTP_POST, [] { stopAll("STOP / session ended"); sendStatus(); });
  server.on("/config", HTTP_POST, handleConfig);
  server.on("/face", HTTP_POST, handleFace);
  server.onNotFound([] { error(404, "Use Scout Android controller / protocol 2"); });
  if (wifiReady) {
    static const char* originHeaders[] = {"Origin"};
    browserSocket.onValidateHttpHeader([](String name, String value) {
      return !name.equalsIgnoreCase("Origin") || value == "http://192.168.4.1";
    }, originHeaders, 1);
    browserSocket.onEvent(socketEvent);
    browserSocket.begin();
    if (xTaskCreate(browserTask, "scout_socket", 8192, nullptr, 1, nullptr) != pdPASS) {
      browserSocket.close(); Serial.println("Browser controls unavailable; Android control remains available");
    }
    server.begin();
    if(xTaskCreate(webTask,"scout_web",8192,nullptr,1,nullptr)!=pdPASS) {
      portENTER_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);control.ready=false;portEXIT_CRITICAL(&safetyMux);stopAll("Web task setup failed / stopped");
    }
  }
  Serial.println("SCOUT 2 | Wi-Fi C3-Scout-Test | 192.168.4.1 | UDP 4210 | x/SPACE stops; ? status");
  Serial.println("RUN OPEN with ESP USB connected. Unplug ESP USB before RUN ON.");
  Serial.println("Browser control: http://192.168.4.1 | WebSocket port 81");
  if (xTaskCreate(oledTask, "scout_oled", 6144, nullptr, 0, nullptr) != pdPASS)
    Serial.println("OLED task unavailable; driving remains available");
}

void loop() {
  safetyTick(nullptr);
  while (Serial.available()) {
    const char c = Serial.read();
    if (c == 'x' || c == 'X' || c == ' ') { stopAll("Serial STOP / session ended"); Serial.println("STOPPED"); }
    else if (c == '?') Serial.println(statusJson());
  }
  receiveDrive(); updateOutputs(); delay(1);
}

package com.scout.control;
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;

final class DriveDatagram {
    static final int PORT = 4210;
    static final String ZERO_TOKEN = "00000000000000000000000000000000";
    static byte[] encode(boolean stop, String token, long sequence, int left, int right) {
        if (token == null || !token.matches("[0-9a-f]{32}") || sequence < 0 || sequence > 0xffffffffL || (!stop && sequence==0) || Math.abs(left)>100 || Math.abs(right)>100)
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid drive packet");
        return ByteBuffer.allocate(45).put(new byte[]{'S','C','T','2'}).put((byte)(stop?'S':'D')).put(token.getBytes(StandardCharsets.US_ASCII))
            .putInt((int)sequence).putShort((short)left).putShort((short)right).array();
    }
    static final class Ack {
        String token; long sequence, boot; int code, flags, left, right;
    }
    static Ack decode(byte[] bytes, int length) {
        if (length != 50 || bytes[0]!='A'||bytes[1]!='C'||bytes[2]!='K'||bytes[3]!='2') return null;
        ByteBuffer b=ByteBuffer.wrap(bytes,0,length);b.position(4);byte[] token=new byte[32];b.get(token);
        Ack a=new Ack();a.token=new String(token,StandardCharsets.US_ASCII);a.sequence=b.getInt()&0xffffffffL;a.code=b.get()&255;
        a.boot=b.getInt()&0xffffffffL;a.flags=b.get()&255;a.left=b.getShort();a.right=b.getShort();
        return a.code<=3&&a.flags<=7&&Math.abs(a.left)<=100&&Math.abs(a.right)<=100 ? a : null;
    }
}

package com.scout.control;

/** Latest-only face requests. Caller holds ScoutClient.state's monitor. */
final class FaceSelection {
    static final String[] NAMES = {"Happy", "Laughing", "Surprised", "Angry", "Sad",
        "Sleepy", "Skeptical", "Winking", "Cheeky", "Dizzy"};
    static final class Ticket {
        final long epoch, generation; final String token; final int id;
        Ticket(long epoch, long generation, String token, int id) {
            this.epoch = epoch; this.generation = generation; this.token = token; this.id = id;
        }
    }
    boolean supported, available, pending;
    int selected = -1;
    long generation;
    String message = "Connect to choose a face";
    void initialize(boolean supported, boolean available, int selection) {
        ++generation; pending = false;
        this.supported = supported; this.available = available;
        selected = selection >= -1 && selection < NAMES.length ? selection : -1;
        message = !supported ? "Firmware update needed for face controls" :
            !available ? "OLED unavailable · check wiring and restart Scout" : label(selected);
    }
    static String label(int id) { return id == -1 ? "Auto · all ten expressions" : NAMES[id]; }
    boolean queue(int id) {
        if (!supported || !available || id < -1 || id >= NAMES.length) return false;
        selected = id; pending = true; ++generation;
        message = "Selecting " + label(id) + "…";
        return true;
    }
    Ticket take(long epoch, String token) {
        if (!pending) return null;
        pending = false;
        return new Ticket(epoch, generation, token, selected);
    }
    boolean current(Ticket ticket, long epoch, boolean active) {
        return active && ticket.epoch == epoch && ticket.generation == generation;
    }
    void clear() {
        ++generation; pending = false; supported = available = false;
        message = "Connect to choose a face";
    }
}

package com.scout.control;

import android.content.Context;
import android.graphics.Canvas;
import android.graphics.Paint;
import android.graphics.Path;
import android.graphics.RadialGradient;
import android.graphics.Shader;
import android.view.MotionEvent;
import android.view.View;

final class JoystickView extends View {
    interface Listener { void move(float forward, float turn, boolean touching); }
    private final Paint paint = new Paint(Paint.ANTI_ALIAS_FLAG);
    private final Listener listener;
    private int pointer = -1;
    private float x, y;
    private boolean driving;
    private final int mint = 0xffa3e9c0;
    JoystickView(Context context, Listener listener) {
        super(context); this.listener = listener;
        setContentDescription("Drive joystick. Drag up to go forward, down to reverse, left or right to turn. Release to stop.");
        setFocusable(true); setImportantForAccessibility(IMPORTANT_FOR_ACCESSIBILITY_YES);
    }
    void ready(boolean value) { driving = value; if (!value) reset(); invalidate(); }
    void reset() { pointer = -1; x = y = 0; invalidate(); }
    private float dp(float value) { return value * getResources().getDisplayMetrics().density; }
    @Override protected void onDraw(Canvas canvas) {
        super.onDraw(canvas);
        float cx = getWidth() / 2f, cy = getHeight() / 2f;
        float radius = Math.max(dp(20), Math.min(getWidth(), getHeight()) / 2f - dp(25));
        paint.setShader(new RadialGradient(cx, cy, radius, new int[] {0xff223c30, 0xff13251d}, null, Shader.TileMode.CLAMP));
        paint.setStyle(Paint.Style.FILL); canvas.drawCircle(cx, cy, radius, paint); paint.setShader(null);
        paint.setStyle(Paint.Style.STROKE); paint.setStrokeWidth(dp(1)); paint.setColor(0xff355044);
        canvas.drawCircle(cx, cy, radius, paint); paint.setColor(0xff294236);
        canvas.drawCircle(cx, cy, radius * .68f, paint); canvas.drawCircle(cx, cy, radius * .34f, paint);
        paint.setColor(0xff365347);
        canvas.drawLine(cx - radius + dp(12), cy, cx + radius - dp(12), cy, paint);
        canvas.drawLine(cx, cy - radius + dp(12), cx, cy + radius - dp(12), paint);
        paint.setStyle(Paint.Style.FILL); paint.setTextAlign(Paint.Align.CENTER);
        paint.setTextSize(dp(10));
        paint.setColor(driving ? 0xffb4d1c1 : 0xff708d7d);
        canvas.drawText("FORWARD", cx, cy - radius - dp(10), paint);
        canvas.drawText("REVERSE", cx, cy + radius + dp(18), paint);
        float travel = radius * .68f;
        float kx = cx + x * travel, ky = cy + y * travel;
        paint.setColor(0x55000000); canvas.drawCircle(kx, ky + dp(5), radius * .23f, paint);
        paint.setColor(driving ? mint : 0xff4f6d5c); canvas.drawCircle(kx, ky, radius * .23f, paint);
        paint.setStyle(Paint.Style.STROKE); paint.setStrokeWidth(dp(1)); paint.setColor(driving ? 0xffd7f7e5 : 0xff789583);
        canvas.drawCircle(kx, ky, radius * .23f - dp(4), paint);
        paint.setStyle(Paint.Style.FILL); paint.setColor(0xff183a28);
        Path arrow = new Path(); float a = radius * .075f;
        arrow.moveTo(kx, ky - a); arrow.lineTo(kx + a, ky + a); arrow.lineTo(kx, ky + a * .45f); arrow.lineTo(kx - a, ky + a); arrow.close();
        canvas.drawPath(arrow, paint);
    }
    @Override public boolean onTouchEvent(MotionEvent event) {
        if (!driving) return true;
        int action = event.getActionMasked();
        if (action == MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN) {
            pointer = event.getPointerId(0); getParent().requestDisallowInterceptTouchEvent(true); sample(event, 0); return true;
        }
        if (action == MotionEvent.ACTION_MOVE && pointer != -1) {
            int index = event.findPointerIndex(pointer); if (index < 0) release(); else sample(event, index); return true;
        }
        if (action == MotionEvent.ACTION_UP || action == MotionEvent.ACTION_CANCEL ||
            (action == MotionEvent.ACTION_POINTER_UP && event.getPointerId(event.getActionIndex()) == pointer)) {
            release(); if (action == MotionEvent.ACTION_UP) performClick(); return true;
        }
        return true;
    }
    private void sample(MotionEvent event, int index) {
        float radius = Math.max(dp(20), Math.min(getWidth(), getHeight()) / 2f - dp(25)) * .68f;
        x = (event.getX(index) - getWidth() / 2f) / radius;
        y = (event.getY(index) - getHeight() / 2f) / radius;
        float length = (float) Math.hypot(x, y); if (length > 1) { x /= length; y /= length; }
        listener.move(-y, x, true); invalidate();
    }
    private void release() { reset(); getParent().requestDisallowInterceptTouchEvent(false); listener.move(0, 0, false); }
    @Override public boolean performClick() { super.performClick(); return true; }
}
